**Called a dumb dog by his parents due to dyslexia, he put on a leather jacket and became the coolest man on Earth.**

Born October 30, 1945, in Manhattan, New York City, today Henry Franklin Winkler turns **81**, cherished worldwide as an American television icon of supreme warmth.

Struggling through severe undiagnosed dyslexia as a boy, Henry was scolded and ridiculed by his parents, who nicknamed him 'dummer Hund' (dumb dog), but he refused to give up on his acting dream, improvising his way through the Yale School of Drama.

When auditioning for *Happy Days* in 1973, producers envisioned a tall blond greaser, but Henry trusted an unorthodox instinct: infusing petty delinquent Arthur Fonzarelli with swagger, chivalry, and an iconic thumbs-up 'Ayy!'.

The Fonz exploded into a global pop-culture phenomenon across eleven seasons, placing his leather jacket in the Smithsonian, before Henry developed the original *MacGyver* and starred in *Arrested Development* and *The Waterboy*.

At age seventy-two, forty-two years after his first nomination, he won his first Primetime Emmy Award for playing acting teacher Gene Cousineau in HBO's *Barry*.

At 81, Henry Winkler proves that kindness and perseverance conquer every label.

**What was Henry Winkler's greatest role: The Fonz in Happy Days, Gene Cousineau in Barry, or Barry Zuckerkorn? Vote below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Henry Winkler's Smithsonian jacket...**

* Henry did not find out he had dyslexia until age thirty-one, when his stepson Jed was diagnosed and Henry realized the same symptoms applied to him, later writing the best-selling *Hank Zipzer* children's book series.
* ABC executives originally banned Fonzie's leather jacket, allowing him to wear it only when standing next to his motorcycle.

Which fact surprised you most?
posts.reel_script: Ridiculed by his parents and called a dumb dog because of undiagnosed dyslexia, Henry Winkler refused to give up. He auditioned for Happy Days, improvised his lines, and created the coolest character in television history as The Fonz, before winning an Emmy for Barry at age seventy-two. Happy eighty-first birthday to a true television treasure. What is your favorite Henry Winkler moment? Tell us below.

posts.caption:
**Working retail in South Los Angeles, she caught John Singleton's eye and became the timeless queen of Black cinema.**

Born October 30, 1970, in Brooklyn, New York, and raised in South Los Angeles, today Nia Talita Long turns **56**, celebrated as an enduring leading lady of modern Hollywood.

Raised by a hardworking single mother who taught printmaking, young Nia studied acting on weekends while balancing shifts at retail stores, dreaming of breaking through an industry that offered few multidimensional roles to young Black women.

Her life changed when visionary director John Singleton cast her as Brandi in the 1991 landmark classic *Boyz n the Hood*, trusting an unorthodox instinct: radiating girl-next-door warmth paired with fierce emotional backbone.

She captured hearts as Will Smith's bride-to-be Lisa Wilkes on *The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air*, headlined beloved comedy hits like *Friday* and *Big Momma's House*, and starred in romantic masterpieces *Love Jones*, *Soul Food*, and *The Best Man*.

A two-time NAACP Image Award winner, she joined the blockbuster Michael Jackson biopic *Michael* portraying family matriarch Katherine Jackson.

At 56, Nia Long remains the golden standard for grace, beauty, and authentic screen magnetism.

**What was Nia Long's ultimate classic movie: Love Jones, The Best Man, Boyz n the Hood, or Friday? Share your vote below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Nia Long's Fresh Prince casting...**

* Jada Pinkett Smith originally auditioned for the role of Will Smith's fiancée Lisa Wilkes on *The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air*, but was considered too short at five feet, leading producers to cast Nia Long instead.
* Nia and Ice Cube have starred together in three separate beloved films: *Boyz n the Hood*, *Friday*, and *Are We There Yet?*.

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: Balancing acting classes with retail shifts in South Los Angeles, Nia Long got her big break when John Singleton cast her in Boyz n the Hood. She captured the world as Lisa on The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air and starred in timeless classics like Love Jones, The Best Man, and Friday. Happy fifty-sixth birthday to a true cinematic queen. What is your absolute favorite Nia Long movie? Let us know below.
posts.reel_caption: From Boyz n the Hood to The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air and Love Jones, Nia Long has been the undisputed queen of cinema for three decades. What was your favorite role of hers? #NiaLong #BoyzNTheHood #FreshPrince #LoveJones #Friday #BornToday

posts.caption:
**Grinding through smoky comedy clubs at seventeen, he traded standup mics for cinema's most iconic crime lineups.**

Born October 30, 1957, in San Francisco, California, today Kevin Elliot Pollak turns **69**, honored as one of American film and television's most versatile character masters.

Beginning standup comedy at just seventeen, Kevin spent a decade touring comedy clubs across the country, sleeping in cheap motels and mastering razor-sharp celebrity impressions before daring to transition into dramatic screen acting.

Rejecting conventional Hollywood leading-man types, Kevin trusted an unorthodox instinct: blending acerbic wit, cynical realism, and lightning-fast comedic timing into unforgettable supporting roles.

He entered cinematic history as cynical robber Todd Hockney in *The Usual Suspects*, Lt. Sam Weinberg in Rob Reiner's *A Few Good Men*, and corrupt casino executive Phillip Green in Martin Scorsese's *Casino*.

For five acclaimed seasons, he delighted modern audiences as passionate garment factory owner Moishe Maisel in Amazon's smash hit *The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel*.

At 69, Kevin Pollak proves that impeccable timing and character dedication always outlast flashy stardom.

**What was Kevin Pollak's greatest performance: The Usual Suspects, A Few Good Men, Casino, or Mrs. Maisel? Vote below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Kevin Pollak's World Series of Poker run...**

* In 2012, Kevin proved his real-life poker skills by competing in the prestigious World Series of Poker Main Event, finishing 134th out of 6,598 players to take home over $52,000.
* During the famous police lineup scene in *The Usual Suspects*, the actors kept breaking into genuine laughter because Benicio del Toro was quietly passing gas between takes.

Which fact surprised you most?
posts.reel_script: Starting standup comedy at seventeen in San Francisco, Kevin Pollak spent ten years touring before Hollywood came calling. He held his own opposite Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson in A Few Good Men, made film history in The Usual Suspects, and charmed audiences on The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel. Happy sixty-ninth birthday to a master of character acting. What is your favorite Kevin Pollak movie? Tell us below.

Born October 30, 1951, in Pasadena, California, today Harry Robinson Hamlin turns **75**, honored as an enduring leading man of Hollywood fantasy and television drama.

The son of an aeronautical engineer, Harry earned dual degrees in drama and psychology from Yale University, honing classical theater chops at the American Conservatory Theater before catching director Stanley Donen's eye.

In 1981, he starred as mythic Greek hero Perseus in Ray Harryhausen's fantasy classic *Clash of the Titans*, performing across stop-motion legends, flying Pegasus, and decapitating Medusa to capture international box-office glory.

He transitioned to prime-time royalty in 1986 as passionate defense attorney Michael Kuzak in Steven Bochco's groundbreaking drama *L.A. Law*, earning three Golden Globe nominations and being named People's 'Sexiest Man Alive'.

He reinvented his dramatic edge with a Primetime Emmy-nominated turn as slick advertising executive Jim Cutler on AMC's *Mad Men*.

At 75, Harry Hamlin remains a versatile, charismatic gentleman of the screen.

When auditioning for Freeform's *Pretty Little Liars*, she originally read for Spencer Hastings and was rejected, but producers called her back months later to read for the bullied-nerd-turned-queen-bee Mona Vanderwaal.

Raised by his mother in a tough Boston neighborhood with three siblings, Michael was an athletic prodigy who discovered theater after an injury, earning acceptance to the prestigious Juilliard School's Drama Division in New York.
